For through all the repairs of the Tabernacle with the wagons, etc., as explained above, through this they draw His indwelling presence below with a firm and strong bond that will not be severed and will never be demolished. Thus, even now, at the latter end of these days, at the end of exile, in the footsteps of the Messiah, in the bitterness of the bitterness of the exile of the soul of these times, nevertheless the true righteous ones will shine within us, so that even now we will know how to strengthen ourselves at every time, in the aspect of “And of the children of Yissachar, who understood the times, to know what Israel should do.”

(Halachos of Washing the Hands for a Meal, halacha 6, item 23)

pairs.he: "אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה"

pairs.he: (מ״ו, ד)

זֶה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁהִבְטִיחַ ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיַעֲקֹב ״אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה״, וּמוּבָן בַּסְּפָרִים שֶׁזֶּה הַפָּסוּק מְרַמֵּז כָּל סוֹד גָּלוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְעִקַּר הוּא גָּלוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, כָּל הָעֲלִיּוֹת וְהַיְרִידוֹת הָעוֹבְרִים עַל אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי, שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר סוֹד הַגָּלוּת וְהַגְּאֻלָּה. שֶׁהַכֹּל בִּבְחִינַת אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת יְרִידָה תַּכְלִית הָעֲלִיָּה, כַּמּוּבָא.
pairs.en: This is the aspect of what the blessed Lord promised Jacob: “I shall descend with you to Egypt, and I shall also bring you up.” It is understood from the books that this verse alludes to the entire secret of Israel’s exile. Principally, it is the exile of the soul—all the ascents and descents that pass over an Israelite person—which is the principal secret of exile and redemption. Everything is in the aspect of “I shall descend with you to Egypt, and I shall also bring you up,” which is the aspect of a descent whose purpose is ascent, as brought there.

pairs.he: וְהָעִקָּר הוּא הַהִתְחַזְּקוּת, שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְהִתְחַזֵּק מְאֹד מְאֹד בְּתֹקֶף הִתְגַּבְּרוּת מְרִירוּת הַיְרִידָה עַד שֶׁנִּדְמֶה שֶׁכִּמְעַט כִּמְעַט חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, שֶׁדַּיְקָא מִשָּׁם יְרַחֵם עָלָיו ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיוֹשִׁיעוֹ וִיקָרְבוֹ אֵלָיו, כִּי לֹא יִטֹּשׁ ה׳ אֶת עַמּוֹ וְכוּ׳. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אִם אָמַרְתִּי מָטָה רַגְלִי חַסְדְּךָ ה׳ יִסְעָדֵנִי וְכוּ׳. וּכְתִיב וָאֹמַר אָבַד נִצְחִי וְתוֹחַלְתִּי מֵה׳ זֹאת אָשִׁיב אֶל לִבִּי עַל כֵּן אוֹחִיל חַסְדֵי ה׳ כִּי לֹא תָמְנוּ כִּי לֹא כָלוּ רַחֲמָיו חֲדָשִׁים לַבְּקָרִים וְכוּ׳ וְכַנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: The principal thing is strengthening oneself: one must strengthen oneself very, very much amid the intense increase of the bitterness of descent, until it seems that it is almost, almost—Heaven forbid. Precisely from there the blessed Lord will have compassion upon him, save him, and bring him near to Him, for “The Lord will not forsake His people,” etc. As it is written, “If I said: My foot has slipped, Your kindness, Lord, will support me,” etc. And it is written, “And I said: My endurance and my hope from the Lord have perished. This I shall bring back to my heart; therefore I shall hope. The kindnesses of the Lord, for we have not ended, for His mercies have not ceased; new each morning,” etc., and as stated above.

pairs.he: וְכֵן בִּפְסוּקִים רַבִּים וּבִפְרָט בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה מְבֹאָר שֶׁדַּיְקָא כְּשֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל הֵם בְּתַכְלִית הַהִתְרַחֲקוּת וְהַצָּרָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אָז דַּיְקָא יֵשׁ סֵבֶר וְתִקְוָה לִישׁוּעָה גְּדוֹלָה. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ עַל פָּסוּק וְעָלָה מִן הָאָרֶץ דַּיְקָא, עַיֵּן שָׁם. וְכֵן הוּא בִּפְרָטִיּוּת בְּכָל אָדָם וּבְכָל זְמַן. כִּי ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ מְהַפֵּךְ הַמַּכָּה לִרְפוּאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה וְכָל זֶה מְרֻמָּז בַּפָּסוּק אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד.
pairs.en: Likewise, in many verses, and particularly in the words of our rabbis, of blessed memory, it is explained that precisely when Israel is at the utmost distance and distress, Heaven forbid, precisely then there is expectation and hope for a great salvation. As explained in the Midrash concerning the verse “And he will ascend from the land”—precisely; see there. It is likewise so in particular with every person and at every time. For the blessed Lord turns the blow into a remedy, as our rabbis, of blessed memory, said. All this is alluded to in the verse “I shall descend.”

pairs.he: רְמָזוּ שֵׁם קָדוֹשׁ הַיּוֹצֵא מִפְּסוּקִים אֵלּוּ וּלְבָאֵר הַדָּבָר יוֹתֵר, כִּי אִיתָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ שֵׁם שֶׁיּוֹצֵא מִפָּסוּק זֶה, אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה, כַּמּוּבָא בַּתְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁבְּסֵפֶר שַׁעֲרֵי צִיּוֹן וּבַתְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בְּלֵיל הוֹשַׁעְנָא רַבָּה אַחַר תְּהִלִּים שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ לְבַקֵּשׁ וּלְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְהִנָּצֵל מִכָּל מִינֵי צָרוֹת בְּכֹחַ הַשֵּׁם הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַיּוֹצֵא מִפָּסוּק זֶה, אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ וְכוּ׳ שֶׁהוּא אמ״י וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם. וְעִנְיַן יְצִיאַת הַשֵּׁם הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַזֶּה הוּא כָּךְ, כִּי בְּפָסוּק זֶה יֵשׁ שְׁלֹשִׁים אוֹתִיּוֹת מִן ״אָנֹכִי״ עַד ״גַם עָלֹה״, וּמְחַלְּקִים אוֹתָם לִשְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים שֶׁל יוּד יוּד יוּד אוֹתִיּוֹת, דְּהַיְנוּ ״אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ״ הוּא יוּד אוֹתִיּוֹת, וְכֵן ״מִצְרַיְמָה״ ״וְאָנֹכִי״ עַד הַיּוּד שֶׁל ״וְאָנֹכִי״ הֵם יוּד אוֹתִיּוֹת, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַיּוּד שֶׁל ״וְאָנֹכִי״ וּתֵבוֹת שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו ״אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה״ הֵם יוּד אוֹתִיּוֹת, וּמְחַבְּרִין אוֹת אַחַת מִכָּל חֵלֶק וְחֵלֶק מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים הַנַּ״ל וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוֹצֵא הַשֵּׁם הַנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: They alluded to a holy Name that emerges from these verses. To explain the matter further: it is stated that there is a Name that emerges from this verse, “I shall descend with you to Egypt,” as brought in the prayers in the book Shaaray Tziyon and in the prayers said on the night of Hoashanuh Rabbuh after Psalms. They ordained requesting and praying to be saved from all kinds of troubles through the power of the holy Name that emerges from this verse, “I shall descend with you,” etc., which is אמ״י, etc.; see there. The manner in which this holy Name emerges is as follows: in this verse there are thirty letters from “אָנֹכִי” through “גַם עָלֹה,” and they divide them into three parts of ten, ten, ten letters. That is, “אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ” is ten letters. Likewise, “מִצְרַיְמָה” and “וְאָנֹכִי,” up to the yud of “וְאָנֹכִי,” are ten letters. Then the yud of “וְאָנֹכִי” and the words after it, “אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה,” are ten letters. They join one letter from each and every part of the three aforesaid parts, and through this the aforesaid Name emerges.

pairs.he: דְּהַיְנוּ הָאָלֶף שֶׁל ״אָנֹכִי״ וְהַמֵּם שֶׁל ״מִצְרַיְמָה״ וְהַיּוּד שֶׁל ״וְאָנֹכִי״ הַנַּ״ל וְיוֹצֵא הַשֵּׁם אמי. וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ הַנּוּן שֶׁל ״אָנֹכִי״ וְהַצַּדִּי שֶׁל ״מִצְרַיְמָה״ וְהָאָלֶף שֶׁל ״אַעַלְךָ״. וְכֵן כֻּלָּם. וְהַסֵּדֶר הוּא כָּךְ (אנכי ארד עמך מצרימה ואנכי אעלך גם עלה).
pairs.en: That is, the alef of “אָנֹכִי,” the mem of “מִצְרַיְמָה,” and the yud of the aforesaid “וְאָנֹכִי,” and the Name אמי emerges. Likewise, afterward, the nun of “אָנֹכִי,” the tzadi of “מִצְרַיְמָה,” and the alef of “אַעַלְךָ.” And likewise all of them. The order is thus (אנכי ארד עמך מצרימה ואנכי אעלך גם עלה).

qualifiedAfter.en: That is, the alef of “אָנֹכִי,” the mem of “מִצְרַיְמָה,” and the yud of the aforesaid “וְאָנֹכִי,” and the Name אמי emerges. Likewise, afterward, the nun of “אָנֹכִי,” the tzadi of “מִצְרַיְמָה,” and the alef of “אַעַלְךָ.” And likewise all of them. The order is thus (אנכי ארד עמך מצרימה ואנכי אעלך גם עלה).

pairs.he: וְהַמֵּשִׂים לֵב יוּכַל לְהָבִין מִזֶּה רְמָזִים נִפְלָאִים לְעִנְיָן הַנַּ״ל לְהִתְחַזֵּק תָּמִיד לִהְיוֹת מְצַפֶּה לִישׁוּעָה גְּדוֹלָה בְּכָל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹר עָלָיו, כִּי יֵשׁ בַּפָּסוּק הַזֶּה שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת, וְהַגָּלוּת בְּעַצְמָהּ, וְהָעֲלִיָּה מִתּוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים, שֶׁהֵם אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת. וּצְרִיכִין לֵידַע וּלְהַאֲמִין שֶׁגַּם בְּעֵת הַיְרִידָה בְּעַצְמָהּ ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ עִמּוֹ בִּבְחִינַת אָנֹכִי בְּעַצְמִי, כִּבְיָכוֹל, אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ. וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַחֵלֶק הַשֵּׁנִי הוּא מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי עַד הַיּוּד, לְרַמֵּז עַל הַגָּלוּת בְּעַצְמָהּ שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מִצְרַיְמָה שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת. וְתֵכֶף כְּשֶׁבָּאִים בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת שֶׁהוּא הַיְרִידָה, תֵּכֶף מַתְחִיל הָעֲלִיָּה וְעַל כֵּן נִכְתַּב מִיָּד, וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ.
pairs.en: One who pays attention can understand from this wondrous allusions concerning the aforesaid matter: to strengthen oneself always to anticipate great salvation through whatever may pass over him. For there are three parts in this verse, which are the aspect of the descent into exile, the exile itself, and the ascent from exile. This is the aspect of three parts, which are “I shall descend with you,” which is the aspect of the descent into exile. One must know and believe that even at the time of the descent itself the blessed Lord is with him, in the aspect of “I Myself, as it were, shall descend with you.” Then the second part is “מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי” up to the yud, to allude to the exile itself, which is the aspect of Egypt, comprising all the exiles. Immediately when one comes into the exile, which is the descent, the ascent immediately begins; therefore it is written at once, “And I shall bring you up.”

pairs.he: נִמְצָא שֶׁאָנֹכִי הָרִאשׁוֹן מְרַמֵּז עַל הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת, וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי מְרַמֵּז עַל הָעֲלִיָּה מִתּוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת, אַךְ בִּשְׁעַת הַגָּלוּת וְהַיְרִידָה כְּשֶׁמַּתְחִיל צְמִיחַת קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִבְּחִינַת וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הָעֲלִיָּה בְּחִינַת וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ וְכוּ׳, אֲזַי הַבַּעַל דָּבָר רוֹצֶה לְהִתְגַּבֵּר בְּיוֹתֵר, כְּדֶרֶךְ שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים הַנִּלְחָמִים זֶה בָּזֶה שֶׁכְּשֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁהָאֶחָד מִתְגַּבֵּר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ אֲזַי הוּא מִתְחַזֵּק כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בְּהִתְגַּבְּרוּת וְהִתְגַּבְּרוּת יוֹתֵר, כַּמּוּבָא בִּדְבָרֵינוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים וְזֶה עִקַּר תֹּקֶף מְרִירוּת הַגָּלוּת שֶׁל עַכְשָׁו מֵחֲמַת שֶׁהוּא עַכְשָׁו בְּעִקְבוֹת מְשִׁיחָא וְה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ מְצַפֶּה בְּכָל יוֹם לְמַהֵר לְגָאֳלֵנוּ, עַל כֵּן מִתְגַּבֵּר בְּיוֹתֵר בִּכְלָל וּבִפְרָט כַּיָּדוּעַ.
pairs.en: It follows that the first “I” alludes to the descent into exile, and the second “I” alludes to ascent from exile. But at the time of exile and descent, when the sprouting of the horn of salvation begins—which is drawn from the aspect of the second “And I,” which is the aspect of ascent, the aspect of “And I shall bring you up,” etc.—then the adversary wishes to overpower all the more. It is as with two people fighting one another: when one sees that the other is gaining strength against him, he then strengthens himself against him with greater and greater exertion, as brought in our words several times. This is the principal intensity of the bitterness of the present exile, because now it is at the heels of the Messiah, and the blessed Lord anticipates each day hastening to redeem us; therefore the adversary gains strength all the more, in general and in particular, as is known.

pairs.he: וְזֶה מְרֻמָּז בְּסוֹד הַשֵּׁם שֶׁל הַפָּסוּק הַנַּ״ל שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל כָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת וּגְאֻלָּתָם בִּכְלָל וּבִפְרָט כַּנַּ״ל, כִּי הַחֵלֶק הַשֵּׁנִי הוּא מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי עַד הַיּוּד הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל וְאָנֹכִי, כִּי וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי הוּא בְּחִינַת הַתִּקְוָה לִישׁוּעָה בְּחִינַת וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה, אַךְ תֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁמַּתְחִיל בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת צְמִיחַת קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִן וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי, אֲזַי הַסִּטְרָא אַחֲרָא וְהַבַּעַל דָּבָר מִתְגַּבְּרִין לְהַעְלִים גַּם זֹאת וְרוֹצִים לִתְפֹּס גַּם בְּחִינַת זֹאת לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת בְּסוֹד גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת שֶׁאוֹתִיּוֹת הָאֶמְצָעִיִּים הֵם ״מִצְרַיְמָה״ ״וְאָנֹכִי״, כִּי גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת רוֹצֶה לְהִתְגַּבֵּר גַּם עַל וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי לְהַעְלִים הַצְּמִיחַת קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִשָּׁם.
pairs.en: This is alluded to in the secret of the Name of the aforesaid verse, which alludes to all the exiles and their redemption, in general and in particular, as stated above. For the second part is “מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי” up to the final yud of “וְאָנֹכִי”; for the second “And I” is the aspect of hope for salvation, the aspect of “And I shall also bring you up.” But immediately when the sprouting of the horn of salvation begins within the exile, which is drawn from the second “And I,” then the other side and the adversary gain strength to conceal this too. They wish to seize this aspect too into the exile, in the secret of the exile of the Divine Presence. This is the aspect of the middle letters being “מִצְרַיְמָה” and “וְאָנֹכִי,” for the Egyptian exile, which comprises all the exiles, wishes to gain strength even against the second “And I,” to conceal the sprouting of the horn of salvation that is drawn from there.

pairs.he: וּמִגֹּדֶל הִתְגַּבְּרוּתָם מְאֹד מְאֹד עַד שֶׁמַּעֲלִימִין וּמַסְתִּירִין הַכֹּל הָיָה כִּמְעַט אֶפֶס תִּקְוָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לוּלֵא ה׳ עֶזְרָתָה לָנוּ שֶׁכְּשֶׁמִּתְפַּשְּׁטִין בְּיוֹתֵר עַל הַקְּדֻשָּׁה וְרוֹצִים לְהַעְלִים לְגַמְרֵי בִּבְחִינַת צוֹפֶה רָשָׁע לַצַּדִּיק וּמְבַקֵּשׁ לַהֲמִיתוֹ, אֲזַי דַּיְקָא ה׳ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בְּסִימָן רז עַל פָּסוּק זֶה, עַיֵּן שָׁם מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב, שֶׁהַסִּטְרָא אַחֲרָא וְהַחוֹלְקִים רוֹצִים לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט לִתְפֹּס הַצַּדִּיק לְגַמְרֵי וְכוּ׳ עַד שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לְהַנְשִׁים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אֲבָל ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ.
pairs.en: Because of their exceedingly, exceedingly great increase of strength, until they conceal and hide everything, there would have been almost no hope, Heaven forbid, had the Lord not come to our aid. When they spread themselves still more against holiness and wish to conceal it completely, in the aspect of “The wicked watches the righteous man and seeks to put him to death,” precisely then “The Lord will not abandon him into his hand.” As explained in section רז concerning this verse: see there what is written, that the other side and the opponents wish to spread themselves to seize the righteous man completely, etc., until he cannot take breath, Heaven forbid. But the blessed Lord will not abandon him into his hand.

pairs.he: וְזֶה סוֹד הַיּוּד הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי, שֶׁהִיא שַׁיָּכָה לְהַחֵלֶק הַשְּׁלִישִׁי הַמִּצְטָרֵף לְתֵבוֹת אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה. לְרַמֵּז שֶׁכְּשֶׁמִּתְפַּשְּׁטִים גַּם עַל וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי וְרוֹצִים לְהַעְלִים הַצְּמִיחַת קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִשָּׁם כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּקְּעוּ בְּגָלוּתָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אֲבָל ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדָם, כִּי יָדוֹ אוֹחֶזֶת בַּעֲקֵב עֵשָׂו כְּתִיב. וּפֵרֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַסְפִּיק לִגְמֹר מַלְכוּתוֹ עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא יַעֲקֹב וְנוֹטְלָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ, כִּי הַיּוּד שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַיּוּד הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי הַנַּ״ל, כְּשֶׁרוֹצִים לְהִתְגַּבֵּר וּלְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט גַּם עָלֶיהָ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְהַעְלִים הַכֹּל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אֲזַי זֹאת הַיּוּד מִתְגַּבֶּרֶת וּמִצְטָרֶפֶת לְתֵבַת אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְהַפֵּךְ הַכֹּל לַעֲלִיָּה גְּדוֹלָה וְכַנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: This is the secret of the final yud of the second “וְאָנֹכִי,” which belongs to the third part and joins the words “אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה.” It alludes to this: when they extend themselves also over the second “And I,” and wish to conceal the sprouting of the horn of salvation drawn from there so that they will become submerged in their exile, Heaven forbid, the blessed Lord will nevertheless not abandon him into their hand. For it is written, “His hand grips Esau’s heel.” Rashi explained that he does not have time to finish his kingship before Jacob comes and takes it from him. For the yud of Jacob, which is the aspect of the final yud of the aforesaid second “וְאָנֹכִי”—when they wish to gain strength and extend themselves even over it, Heaven forbid, to conceal everything, Heaven forbid—then this yud gains strength and joins the expression “אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה,” through which everything is transformed into a great ascent, as stated above.

pairs.he: וְהָבֵן הַדָּבָר הֵיטֵב, כִּי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּחַלְּקִים הַפָּסוּק לִשְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים כַּנַּ״ל, שֶׁהֵם הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת וְהַגָּלוּת בְּעַצְמוֹ וְהָעֲלִיָּה מִתּוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת, אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל נִכְלָל בִּשְׁתֵּי בְּחִינוֹת. כִּי תֵכֶף כְּשֶׁבָּאִים בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת תֵּכֶף מַתְחִיל צְמִיחַת קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה, כִּי מַתְחִיל מִיָּד הָעֲלִיָּה. שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת מִלּוּי פְּגִימַת הַלְּבָנָה שֶׁתֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁבָּאָה לְתַכְלִית הַמִּעוּט מַתְחֶלֶת לְהִתְמַלֹּאות מִיָּד, שֶׁזֶּה מְרַמֵּז עַל הַגְּאֻלָּה מִתּוֹךְ תֹּקֶף הַגָּלוּת כַּיָּדוּעַ. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כִּי יִרְאֶה כִּי אָזְלַת יָד וְאֶפֶס עָצוּר וְעָזוּב וְכוּ׳ רְאוּ עַתָּה כִּי אֲנִי אֲנִי הוּא וְכוּ׳.
pairs.en: Understand the matter well: although the verse is divided into three parts, as stated above—the descent into exile, the exile itself, and the ascent from exile—in truth, everything is included in two aspects. Immediately when one comes into exile, the sprouting of the horn of salvation begins immediately, for the ascent begins at once. This is the aspect of filling the moon’s deficiency: immediately when it comes to the utmost diminution, it begins at once to fill. This alludes to redemption from the intensity of exile, as is known. As it is written, “For He will see that strength has departed, and that there is none confined or free,” etc., “See now that I, I am He,” etc.

pairs.en: In very truth everything is one, for the descent itself is the ascent, in the aspect of a descent whose purpose is ascent. But the principal exile is the exile of knowledge, which wishes to hide and conceal knowledge completely, as though there were no hope, Heaven forbid, as it is written, “With murder in my bones my foes have taunted me, saying to me all day: Where is your God?” etc. Likewise in many verses, until they wish to conceal even the second “And I,” which is the beginning of the sprouting of the horn of salvation, as stated above. But when he wishes to conceal and hide it completely, the Lord will not abandon him into his hand; for the final yud in the second “וְאָנֹכִי” gains strength and joins the words “אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה,” and everything is transformed into a great ascent, as stated above.

pairs.he: כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל לְהֵפֶךְ, כִּי ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ עִמּוֹ תָּמִיד בֵּין בְּעֵת הַיְרִידָה בֵּין בְּהַגָּלוּת בְּעַצְמוֹ בֵּין בְּעֵת הָעֲלִיָּה כִּמְפֹרָשׁ בַּפָּסוּק זֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ, וְאָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ וְכוּ׳. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב, אִתִּי מִלְּבָנוֹן כַּלָּה אִתִּי מִלְּבָנוֹן תָּבוֹאִי וְכוּ׳. וְעַיֵּן פֵּרוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י שָׁם שֶׁפֵּרֵשׁ מַה שֶּׁלֹּא כְּתִיב אִתִּי לַלְּבָנוֹן תָּבוֹאִי, לוֹמַר, מִשְּׁעַת יְצִיאַתְכֶם מִכָּאן, עַד שְׁעַת בִּיאָתְכֶם לְכָאן אֲנִי עִמָּכֶם בְּכָל אֲשֶׁר תֵּצְאוּ וְתָבוֹאוּ, הַיְנוּ כַּנַּ״ל וְהָבֵן הֵיטֵב.
pairs.en: For in truth everything is the opposite: the blessed Lord is with him always, whether at the time of descent, in the exile itself, or at the time of ascent, as expressly stated in this very verse: “And I shall descend with you to Egypt, and I shall bring you up,” etc. As it is written, “With Me from Lebanon, bride, with Me from Lebanon you shall come,” etc. Examine Rashi’s commentary there, where he explained why it is not written “With Me to Lebanon you shall come”: to say, from the time of your departure from here until the time of your coming here, I am with you wherever you go out and come in. That is, as stated above; understand well.

pairs.en: If you examine more closely, you will see wonders. For surely the yud of the aforesaid “וְאָנֹכִי,” which joins the expression “אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה,” from which comes the principal ascent—for it is what stood by us and our forefathers in our exile, not allowing the other side to spread even over it, etc., as stated above—this very yud joins in the first Name that emerges from this verse, which is אמ״י: the alef of the first “אָנֹכִי,” the mem of “מִצְרַיְמָה,” and this aforesaid yud, as stated above.

pairs.he: נִמְצָא שֶׁגַּם בְּהַתְחָלַת הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ וּמֵהַתְחָלַת הַגָּלוּת הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַמֵּם שֶׁהִיא אוֹת רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁל מִצְרַיְמָה שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַגָּלוּת תֵּכֶף וּמִיָּד נִצְטָרֵף שָׁם הַיּוּד הַנַּ״ל שֶׁהִיא יוּד הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל וְאָנֹכִי שֵׁנִי הַנַּ״ל שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הַתִּקְוָה וְהָעֲלִיָּה כַּנַּ״ל וְנַעֲשֶׂה הַשֵּׁם אמ״י כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: It follows that even at the beginning of the descent into exile, which is the aspect of “I shall descend with you,” and from the beginning of the first exile itself—which is the aspect of the mem, the first letter of “מִצְרַיְמָה,” which is the beginning of exile—immediately and at once the aforesaid yud is joined there. It is the final yud of the aforesaid second “וְאָנֹכִי,” from which come hope and ascent, as stated above; and the Name אמ״י is formed, as stated above.

pairs.he: כָּל זֶה לְהוֹדִיעַ וּלְהוֹרוֹת שֶׁגַּם בְּהַתְחָלַת הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת וּבְהַתְחָלַת הַגָּלוּת תֵּכֶף עָמְדָה לָנוּ הַיּוּד הַנַּ״ל שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הָעֲלִיָּה וְהִיא בְּעַצְמָהּ עָמְדָה לָנוּ בְּהַתְחָלַת הַיְרִידָה וְהַגָּלוּת בְּעַצְמָהּ לְשָׁמְרֵנוּ וּלְהַצִּילֵנוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ שָׁם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כִּי ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ מַגִּיד מֵרֵאשִׁית אַחֲרִית, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ עַל פָּסוּק. וַיְהִי בָעֵת הַהִיא וַיֵּרֶד יְהוּדָה וְכוּ׳, שֶׁעַד שֶׁלֹּא הִתְחִיל הַגָּלוּת הָרִאשׁוֹן נוֹלַד הַגּוֹאֵל הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁהוּא פֶרֶץ וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם, הַיְנוּ כַּנַּ״ל וְהָבֵן.
pairs.en: All this is to make known and teach that even at the beginning of the descent into exile and at the beginning of exile, the aforesaid yud, from which comes ascent, immediately stood by us. "אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה"

(מ״ו, ד)

זֶה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁהִבְטִיחַ ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיַעֲקֹב ״אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה״, וּמוּבָן בַּסְּפָרִים שֶׁזֶּה הַפָּסוּק מְרַמֵּז כָּל סוֹד גָּלוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְעִקַּר הוּא גָּלוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, כָּל הָעֲלִיּוֹת וְהַיְרִידוֹת הָעוֹבְרִים עַל אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי, שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר סוֹד הַגָּלוּת וְהַגְּאֻלָּה. שֶׁהַכֹּל בִּבְחִינַת אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת יְרִידָה תַּכְלִית הָעֲלִיָּה, כַּמּוּבָא.

וְהָעִקָּר הוּא הַהִתְחַזְּקוּת, שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְהִתְחַזֵּק מְאֹד מְאֹד בְּתֹקֶף הִתְגַּבְּרוּת מְרִירוּת הַיְרִידָה עַד שֶׁנִּדְמֶה שֶׁכִּמְעַט כִּמְעַט חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, שֶׁדַּיְקָא מִשָּׁם יְרַחֵם עָלָיו ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיוֹשִׁיעוֹ וִיקָרְבוֹ אֵלָיו, כִּי לֹא יִטֹּשׁ ה׳ אֶת עַמּוֹ וְכוּ׳. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אִם אָמַרְתִּי מָטָה רַגְלִי חַסְדְּךָ ה׳ יִסְעָדֵנִי וְכוּ׳. וּכְתִיב וָאֹמַר אָבַד נִצְחִי וְתוֹחַלְתִּי מֵה׳ זֹאת אָשִׁיב אֶל לִבִּי עַל כֵּן אוֹחִיל חַסְדֵי ה׳ כִּי לֹא תָמְנוּ כִּי לֹא כָלוּ רַחֲמָיו חֲדָשִׁים לַבְּקָרִים וְכוּ׳ וְכַנַּ״ל.

וְכֵן בִּפְסוּקִים רַבִּים וּבִפְרָט בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה מְבֹאָר שֶׁדַּיְקָא כְּשֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל הֵם בְּתַכְלִית הַהִתְרַחֲקוּת וְהַצָּרָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אָז דַּיְקָא יֵשׁ סֵבֶר וְתִקְוָה לִישׁוּעָה גְּדוֹלָה. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ עַל פָּסוּק וְעָלָה מִן הָאָרֶץ דַּיְקָא, עַיֵּן שָׁם. וְכֵן הוּא בִּפְרָטִיּוּת בְּכָל אָדָם וּבְכָל זְמַן. כִּי ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ מְהַפֵּךְ הַמַּכָּה לִרְפוּאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה וְכָל זֶה מְרֻמָּז בַּפָּסוּק אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד.

רְמָזוּ שֵׁם קָדוֹשׁ הַיּוֹצֵא מִפְּסוּקִים אֵלּוּ וּלְבָאֵר הַדָּבָר יוֹתֵר, כִּי אִיתָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ שֵׁם שֶׁיּוֹצֵא מִפָּסוּק זֶה, אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה, כַּמּוּבָא בַּתְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁבְּסֵפֶר שַׁעֲרֵי צִיּוֹן וּבַתְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בְּלֵיל הוֹשַׁעְנָא רַבָּה אַחַר תְּהִלִּים שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ לְבַקֵּשׁ וּלְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְהִנָּצֵל מִכָּל מִינֵי צָרוֹת בְּכֹחַ הַשֵּׁם הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַיּוֹצֵא מִפָּסוּק זֶה, אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ וְכוּ׳ שֶׁהוּא אמ״י וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם. וְעִנְיַן יְצִיאַת הַשֵּׁם הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַזֶּה הוּא כָּךְ, כִּי בְּפָסוּק זֶה יֵשׁ שְׁלֹשִׁים אוֹתִיּוֹת מִן ״אָנֹכִי״ עַד ״גַם עָלֹה״, וּמְחַלְּקִים אוֹתָם לִשְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים שֶׁל יוּד יוּד יוּד אוֹתִיּוֹת, דְּהַיְנוּ ״אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ״ הוּא יוּד אוֹתִיּוֹת, וְכֵן ״מִצְרַיְמָה״ ״וְאָנֹכִי״ עַד הַיּוּד שֶׁל ״וְאָנֹכִי״ הֵם יוּד אוֹתִיּוֹת, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַיּוּד שֶׁל ״וְאָנֹכִי״ וּתֵבוֹת שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו ״אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה״ הֵם יוּד אוֹתִיּוֹת, וּמְחַבְּרִין אוֹת אַחַת מִכָּל חֵלֶק וְחֵלֶק מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים הַנַּ״ל וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוֹצֵא הַשֵּׁם הַנַּ״ל.

דְּהַיְנוּ הָאָלֶף שֶׁל ״אָנֹכִי״ וְהַמֵּם שֶׁל ״מִצְרַיְמָה״ וְהַיּוּד שֶׁל ״וְאָנֹכִי״ הַנַּ״ל וְיוֹצֵא הַשֵּׁם אמי. וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ הַנּוּן שֶׁל ״אָנֹכִי״ וְהַצַּדִּי שֶׁל ״מִצְרַיְמָה״ וְהָאָלֶף שֶׁל ״אַעַלְךָ״. וְכֵן כֻּלָּם. וְהַסֵּדֶר הוּא כָּךְ (אנכי ארד עמך מצרימה ואנכי אעלך גם עלה).

וְהַמֵּשִׂים לֵב יוּכַל לְהָבִין מִזֶּה רְמָזִים נִפְלָאִים לְעִנְיָן הַנַּ״ל לְהִתְחַזֵּק תָּמִיד לִהְיוֹת מְצַפֶּה לִישׁוּעָה גְּדוֹלָה בְּכָל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹר עָלָיו, כִּי יֵשׁ בַּפָּסוּק הַזֶּה שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת, וְהַגָּלוּת בְּעַצְמָהּ, וְהָעֲלִיָּה מִתּוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים, שֶׁהֵם אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת. וּצְרִיכִין לֵידַע וּלְהַאֲמִין שֶׁגַּם בְּעֵת הַיְרִידָה בְּעַצְמָהּ ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ עִמּוֹ בִּבְחִינַת אָנֹכִי בְּעַצְמִי, כִּבְיָכוֹל, אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ. וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַחֵלֶק הַשֵּׁנִי הוּא מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי עַד הַיּוּד, לְרַמֵּז עַל הַגָּלוּת בְּעַצְמָהּ שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מִצְרַיְמָה שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת. וְתֵכֶף כְּשֶׁבָּאִים בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת שֶׁהוּא הַיְרִידָה, תֵּכֶף מַתְחִיל הָעֲלִיָּה וְעַל כֵּן נִכְתַּב מִיָּד, וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ.

נִמְצָא שֶׁאָנֹכִי הָרִאשׁוֹן מְרַמֵּז עַל הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת, וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי מְרַמֵּז עַל הָעֲלִיָּה מִתּוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת, אַךְ בִּשְׁעַת הַגָּלוּת וְהַיְרִידָה כְּשֶׁמַּתְחִיל צְמִיחַת קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִבְּחִינַת וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הָעֲלִיָּה בְּחִינַת וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ וְכוּ׳, אֲזַי הַבַּעַל דָּבָר רוֹצֶה לְהִתְגַּבֵּר בְּיוֹתֵר, כְּדֶרֶךְ שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים הַנִּלְחָמִים זֶה בָּזֶה שֶׁכְּשֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁהָאֶחָד מִתְגַּבֵּר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ אֲזַי הוּא מִתְחַזֵּק כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בְּהִתְגַּבְּרוּת וְהִתְגַּבְּרוּת יוֹתֵר, כַּמּוּבָא בִּדְבָרֵינוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים וְזֶה עִקַּר תֹּקֶף מְרִירוּת הַגָּלוּת שֶׁל עַכְשָׁו מֵחֲמַת שֶׁהוּא עַכְשָׁו בְּעִקְבוֹת מְשִׁיחָא וְה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ מְצַפֶּה בְּכָל יוֹם לְמַהֵר לְגָאֳלֵנוּ, עַל כֵּן מִתְגַּבֵּר בְּיוֹתֵר בִּכְלָל וּבִפְרָט כַּיָּדוּעַ.

וְזֶה מְרֻמָּז בְּסוֹד הַשֵּׁם שֶׁל הַפָּסוּק הַנַּ״ל שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל כָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת וּגְאֻלָּתָם בִּכְלָל וּבִפְרָט כַּנַּ״ל, כִּי הַחֵלֶק הַשֵּׁנִי הוּא מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי עַד הַיּוּד הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל וְאָנֹכִי, כִּי וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי הוּא בְּחִינַת הַתִּקְוָה לִישׁוּעָה בְּחִינַת וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה, אַךְ תֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁמַּתְחִיל בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת צְמִיחַת קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִן וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי, אֲזַי הַסִּטְרָא אַחֲרָא וְהַבַּעַל דָּבָר מִתְגַּבְּרִין לְהַעְלִים גַּם זֹאת וְרוֹצִים לִתְפֹּס גַּם בְּחִינַת זֹאת לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת בְּסוֹד גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת שֶׁאוֹתִיּוֹת הָאֶמְצָעִיִּים הֵם ״מִצְרַיְמָה״ ״וְאָנֹכִי״, כִּי גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת רוֹצֶה לְהִתְגַּבֵּר גַּם עַל וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי לְהַעְלִים הַצְּמִיחַת קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִשָּׁם.

וּמִגֹּדֶל הִתְגַּבְּרוּתָם מְאֹד מְאֹד עַד שֶׁמַּעֲלִימִין וּמַסְתִּירִין הַכֹּל הָיָה כִּמְעַט אֶפֶס תִּקְוָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לוּלֵא ה׳ עֶזְרָתָה לָנוּ שֶׁכְּשֶׁמִּתְפַּשְּׁטִין בְּיוֹתֵר עַל הַקְּדֻשָּׁה וְרוֹצִים לְהַעְלִים לְגַמְרֵי בִּבְחִינַת צוֹפֶה רָשָׁע לַצַּדִּיק וּמְבַקֵּשׁ לַהֲמִיתוֹ, אֲזַי דַּיְקָא ה׳ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בְּסִימָן רז עַל פָּסוּק זֶה, עַיֵּן שָׁם מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב, שֶׁהַסִּטְרָא אַחֲרָא וְהַחוֹלְקִים רוֹצִים לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט לִתְפֹּס הַצַּדִּיק לְגַמְרֵי וְכוּ׳ עַד שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לְהַנְשִׁים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אֲבָל ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ.

וְזֶה סוֹד הַיּוּד הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי, שֶׁהִיא שַׁיָּכָה לְהַחֵלֶק הַשְּׁלִישִׁי הַמִּצְטָרֵף לְתֵבוֹת אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה. לְרַמֵּז שֶׁכְּשֶׁמִּתְפַּשְּׁטִים גַּם עַל וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי וְרוֹצִים לְהַעְלִים הַצְּמִיחַת קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִשָּׁם כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּקְּעוּ בְּגָלוּתָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אֲבָל ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדָם, כִּי יָדוֹ אוֹחֶזֶת בַּעֲקֵב עֵשָׂו כְּתִיב. וּפֵרֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַסְפִּיק לִגְמֹר מַלְכוּתוֹ עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא יַעֲקֹב וְנוֹטְלָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ, כִּי הַיּוּד שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַיּוּד הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי הַנַּ״ל, כְּשֶׁרוֹצִים לְהִתְגַּבֵּר וּלְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט גַּם עָלֶיהָ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְהַעְלִים הַכֹּל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אֲזַי זֹאת הַיּוּד מִתְגַּבֶּרֶת וּמִצְטָרֶפֶת לְתֵבַת אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְהַפֵּךְ הַכֹּל לַעֲלִיָּה גְּדוֹלָה וְכַנַּ״ל.

וְהָבֵן הַדָּבָר הֵיטֵב, כִּי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּחַלְּקִים הַפָּסוּק לִשְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים כַּנַּ״ל, שֶׁהֵם הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת וְהַגָּלוּת בְּעַצְמוֹ וְהָעֲלִיָּה מִתּוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת, אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל נִכְלָל בִּשְׁתֵּי בְּחִינוֹת. כִּי תֵכֶף כְּשֶׁבָּאִים בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת תֵּכֶף מַתְחִיל צְמִיחַת קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה, כִּי מַתְחִיל מִיָּד הָעֲלִיָּה. שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת מִלּוּי פְּגִימַת הַלְּבָנָה שֶׁתֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁבָּאָה לְתַכְלִית הַמִּעוּט מַתְחֶלֶת לְהִתְמַלֹּאות מִיָּד, שֶׁזֶּה מְרַמֵּז עַל הַגְּאֻלָּה מִתּוֹךְ תֹּקֶף הַגָּלוּת כַּיָּדוּעַ. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כִּי יִרְאֶה כִּי אָזְלַת יָד וְאֶפֶס עָצוּר וְעָזוּב וְכוּ׳ רְאוּ עַתָּה כִּי אֲנִי אֲנִי הוּא וְכוּ׳.

וּבֶאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ הַכֹּל אֶחָד, כִּי הַיְרִידָה בְּעַצְמָהּ הִיא הָעֲלִיָּה בִּבְחִינַת יְרִידָה תַּכְלִית הָעֲלִיָּה, אַךְ עִקַּר הַגָּלוּת הוּא גָּלוּת הַדַּעַת שֶׁרוֹצָה לְהַסְתִּיר וּלְהַעְלִים הַדַּעַת לְגַמְרֵי כְּאִלּוּ אֶפֶס תִּקְוָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֶצַח בְּעַצְמוֹתַי חֵרְפוּנִי צוֹרְרָי בְּאָמְרָם אֵלַי כָּל הַיּוֹם אַיֵּה אֱלֹקֶיךָ וְכוּ׳. וְכֵן בִּפְסוּקִים הַרְבֵּה, עַד שֶׁרוֹצִים לְהַעְלִים גַּם וְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת צְמִיחַת קֶרֶן יְשׁוּעָה כַּנַּ״ל, אֲבָל כְּשֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהַעְלִים וּלְהַסְתִּיר לְגַמְרֵי ה׳ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ, כִּי הַיּוּד הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבְּוְאָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁנִי מִתְגַּבֶּרֶת וּמִצְטָרֶפֶת עִם תֵּבוֹת אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה וְנִתְהַפֵּךְ הַכֹּל לַעֲלִיָּה גְּדוֹלָה כַּנַּ״ל.

כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל לְהֵפֶךְ, כִּי ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ עִמּוֹ תָּמִיד בֵּין בְּעֵת הַיְרִידָה בֵּין בְּהַגָּלוּת בְּעַצְמוֹ בֵּין בְּעֵת הָעֲלִיָּה כִּמְפֹרָשׁ בַּפָּסוּק זֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ, וְאָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ וְכוּ׳. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב, אִתִּי מִלְּבָנוֹן כַּלָּה אִתִּי מִלְּבָנוֹן תָּבוֹאִי וְכוּ׳. וְעַיֵּן פֵּרוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י שָׁם שֶׁפֵּרֵשׁ מַה שֶּׁלֹּא כְּתִיב אִתִּי לַלְּבָנוֹן תָּבוֹאִי, לוֹמַר, מִשְּׁעַת יְצִיאַתְכֶם מִכָּאן, עַד שְׁעַת בִּיאָתְכֶם לְכָאן אֲנִי עִמָּכֶם בְּכָל אֲשֶׁר תֵּצְאוּ וְתָבוֹאוּ, הַיְנוּ כַּנַּ״ל וְהָבֵן הֵיטֵב.

וְאִם תְּדַקְדֵּק יוֹתֵר תִּרְאֶה נִפְלָאוֹת, כִּי הֲלֹא הַיּוּד שֶׁל וְאָנֹכִי הַנַּ״ל שֶׁהִיא מִצְטָרֶפֶת לְתֵבַת אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה שֶׁמִּשָּׁם עִקַּר הָעֲלִיָּה, כִּי הוּא שֶׁעָמְדָה לָנוּ וְלַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְּגָלוּתֵנוּ שֶׁאֵינָהּ מַנַּחַת שֶׁתִּתְפַּשֵּׁט הַסִּטְרָא אַחֲרָא גַּם עָלֶיהָ וְכוּ׳ וְכַנַּ״ל, זֹאת הַיּוּד בְּעַצְמָהּ מִצְטָרֶפֶת בְּהַשֵּׁם הָרִאשׁוֹן הַיּוֹצֵא מִפָּסוּק זֶה שֶׁהוּא אמ״י, שֶׁהוּא הָאָלֶף שֶׁל ״אָנֹכִי״ הָרִאשׁוֹן וְהַמֵּם שֶׁל ״מִצְרַיְמָה״ וְהַיּוּד הַזֹּאת הַנַּ״ל כַּנַּ״ל.

נִמְצָא שֶׁגַּם בְּהַתְחָלַת הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ וּמֵהַתְחָלַת הַגָּלוּת הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַמֵּם שֶׁהִיא אוֹת רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁל מִצְרַיְמָה שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַגָּלוּת תֵּכֶף וּמִיָּד נִצְטָרֵף שָׁם הַיּוּד הַנַּ״ל שֶׁהִיא יוּד הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל וְאָנֹכִי שֵׁנִי הַנַּ״ל שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הַתִּקְוָה וְהָעֲלִיָּה כַּנַּ״ל וְנַעֲשֶׂה הַשֵּׁם אמ״י כַּנַּ״ל.

כָּל זֶה לְהוֹדִיעַ וּלְהוֹרוֹת שֶׁגַּם בְּהַתְחָלַת הַיְרִידָה לְתוֹךְ הַגָּלוּת וּבְהַתְחָלַת הַגָּלוּת תֵּכֶף עָמְדָה לָנוּ הַיּוּד הַנַּ״ל שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הָעֲלִיָּה וְהִיא בְּעַצְמָהּ עָמְדָה לָנוּ בְּהַתְחָלַת הַיְרִידָה וְהַגָּלוּת בְּעַצְמָהּ לְשָׁמְרֵנוּ וּלְהַצִּילֵנוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ שָׁם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כִּי ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ מַגִּיד מֵרֵאשִׁית אַחֲרִית, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ עַל פָּסוּק. וַיְהִי בָעֵת הַהִיא וַיֵּרֶד יְהוּדָה וְכוּ׳, שֶׁעַד שֶׁלֹּא הִתְחִיל הַגָּלוּת הָרִאשׁוֹן נוֹלַד הַגּוֹאֵל הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁהוּא פֶרֶץ וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם, הַיְנוּ כַּנַּ״ל וְהָבֵן.

(הלכות שלוח הקן הלכה ה׳ אות כ״ג)
breslov.en:
Teaching concerning the descents that will be before the ascents.

“I shall descend with you to Egypt, and I shall also bring you up.”

(46:4)

This is the aspect of what the blessed Lord promised Jacob: “I shall descend with you to Egypt, and I shall also bring you up.” It is understood from the books that this verse alludes to the entire secret of Israel’s exile. Principally, it is the exile of the soul—all the ascents and descents that pass over an Israelite person—which is the principal secret of exile and redemption. Everything is in the aspect of “I shall descend with you to Egypt, and I shall also bring you up,” which is the aspect of a descent whose purpose is ascent, as brought there.

The principal thing is strengthening oneself: one must strengthen oneself very, very much amid the intense increase of the bitterness of descent, until it seems that it is almost, almost—Heaven forbid. Precisely from there the blessed Lord will have compassion upon him, save him, and bring him near to Him, for “The Lord will not forsake His people,” etc. As it is written, “If I said: My foot has slipped, Your kindness, Lord, will support me,” etc. And it is written, “And I said: My endurance and my hope from the Lord have perished. This I shall bring back to my heart; therefore I shall hope. The kindnesses of the Lord, for we have not ended, for His mercies have not ceased; new each morning,” etc., and as stated above.

Likewise, in many verses, and particularly in the words of our rabbis, of blessed memory, it is explained that precisely when Israel is at the utmost distance and distress, Heaven forbid, precisely then there is expectation and hope for a great salvation. As explained in the Midrash concerning the verse “And he will ascend from the land”—precisely; see there. It is likewise so in particular with every person and at every time. For the blessed Lord turns the blow into a remedy, as our rabbis, of blessed memory, said. All this is alluded to in the verse “I shall descend.”

They alluded to a holy Name that emerges from these verses. To explain the matter further: it is stated that there is a Name that emerges from this verse, “I shall descend with you to Egypt,” as brought in the prayers in the book Shaaray Tziyon and in the prayers said on the night of Hoashanuh Rabbuh after Psalms. They ordained requesting and praying to be saved from all kinds of troubles through the power of the holy Name that emerges from this verse, “I shall descend with you,” etc., which is אמ״י, etc.; see there. The manner in which this holy Name emerges is as follows: in this verse there are thirty letters from “אָנֹכִי” through “גַם עָלֹה,” and they divide them into three parts of ten, ten, ten letters. That is, “אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ” is ten letters. Likewise, “מִצְרַיְמָה” and “וְאָנֹכִי,” up to the yud of “וְאָנֹכִי,” are ten letters. Then the yud of “וְאָנֹכִי” and the words after it, “אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה,” are ten letters. They join one letter from each and every part of the three aforesaid parts, and through this the aforesaid Name emerges.

That is, the alef of “אָנֹכִי,” the mem of “מִצְרַיְמָה,” and the yud of the aforesaid “וְאָנֹכִי,” and the Name אמי emerges. Likewise, afterward, the nun of “אָנֹכִי,” the tzadi of “מִצְרַיְמָה,” and the alef of “אַעַלְךָ.” And likewise all of them. The order is thus (אנכי ארד עמך מצרימה ואנכי אעלך גם עלה).

One who pays attention can understand from this wondrous allusions concerning the aforesaid matter: to strengthen oneself always to anticipate great salvation through whatever may pass over him. For there are three parts in this verse, which are the aspect of the descent into exile, the exile itself, and the ascent from exile. This is the aspect of three parts, which are “I shall descend with you,” which is the aspect of the descent into exile. One must know and believe that even at the time of the descent itself the blessed Lord is with him, in the aspect of “I Myself, as it were, shall descend with you.” Then the second part is “מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי” up to the yud, to allude to the exile itself, which is the aspect of Egypt, comprising all the exiles. Immediately when one comes into the exile, which is the descent, the ascent immediately begins; therefore it is written at once, “And I shall bring you up.”

It follows that the first “I” alludes to the descent into exile, and the second “I” alludes to ascent from exile. But at the time of exile and descent, when the sprouting of the horn of salvation begins—which is drawn from the aspect of the second “And I,” which is the aspect of ascent, the aspect of “And I shall bring you up,” etc.—then the adversary wishes to overpower all the more. It is as with two people fighting one another: when one sees that the other is gaining strength against him, he then strengthens himself against him with greater and greater exertion, as brought in our words several times. This is the principal intensity of the bitterness of the present exile, because now it is at the heels of the Messiah, and the blessed Lord anticipates each day hastening to redeem us; therefore the adversary gains strength all the more, in general and in particular, as is known.

This is alluded to in the secret of the Name of the aforesaid verse, which alludes to all the exiles and their redemption, in general and in particular, as stated above. For the second part is “מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי” up to the final yud of “וְאָנֹכִי”; for the second “And I” is the aspect of hope for salvation, the aspect of “And I shall also bring you up.” But immediately when the sprouting of the horn of salvation begins within the exile, which is drawn from the second “And I,” then the other side and the adversary gain strength to conceal this too. They wish to seize this aspect too into the exile, in the secret of the exile of the Divine Presence. This is the aspect of the middle letters being “מִצְרַיְמָה” and “וְאָנֹכִי,” for the Egyptian exile, which comprises all the exiles, wishes to gain strength even against the second “And I,” to conceal the sprouting of the horn of salvation that is drawn from there.

Because of their exceedingly, exceedingly great increase of strength, until they conceal and hide everything, there would have been almost no hope, Heaven forbid, had the Lord not come to our aid. When they spread themselves still more against holiness and wish to conceal it completely, in the aspect of “The wicked watches the righteous man and seeks to put him to death,” precisely then “The Lord will not abandon him into his hand.” As explained in section רז concerning this verse: see there what is written, that the other side and the opponents wish to spread themselves to seize the righteous man completely, etc., until he cannot take breath, Heaven forbid. But the blessed Lord will not abandon him into his hand.

This is the secret of the final yud of the second “וְאָנֹכִי,” which belongs to the third part and joins the words “אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה.” It alludes to this: when they extend themselves also over the second “And I,” and wish to conceal the sprouting of the horn of salvation drawn from there so that they will become submerged in their exile, Heaven forbid, the blessed Lord will nevertheless not abandon him into their hand. For it is written, “His hand grips Esau’s heel.” Rashi explained that he does not have time to finish his kingship before Jacob comes and takes it from him. For the yud of Jacob, which is the aspect of the final yud of the aforesaid second “וְאָנֹכִי”—when they wish to gain strength and extend themselves even over it, Heaven forbid, to conceal everything, Heaven forbid—then this yud gains strength and joins the expression “אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה,” through which everything is transformed into a great ascent, as stated above.

Understand the matter well: although the verse is divided into three parts, as stated above—the descent into exile, the exile itself, and the ascent from exile—in truth, everything is included in two aspects. Immediately when one comes into exile, the sprouting of the horn of salvation begins immediately, for the ascent begins at once. This is the aspect of filling the moon’s deficiency: immediately when it comes to the utmost diminution, it begins at once to fill. This alludes to redemption from the intensity of exile, as is known. As it is written, “For He will see that strength has departed, and that there is none confined or free,” etc., “See now that I, I am He,” etc.

In very truth everything is one, for the descent itself is the ascent, in the aspect of a descent whose purpose is ascent. But the principal exile is the exile of knowledge, which wishes to hide and conceal knowledge completely, as though there were no hope, Heaven forbid, as it is written, “With murder in my bones my foes have taunted me, saying to me all day: Where is your God?” etc. Likewise in many verses, until they wish to conceal even the second “And I,” which is the beginning of the sprouting of the horn of salvation, as stated above. But when he wishes to conceal and hide it completely, the Lord will not abandon him into his hand; for the final yud in the second “וְאָנֹכִי” gains strength and joins the words “אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה,” and everything is transformed into a great ascent, as stated above.

For in truth everything is the opposite: the blessed Lord is with him always, whether at the time of descent, in the exile itself, or at the time of ascent, as expressly stated in this very verse: “And I shall descend with you to Egypt, and I shall bring you up,” etc. As it is written, “With Me from Lebanon, bride, with Me from Lebanon you shall come,” etc. Examine Rashi’s commentary there, where he explained why it is not written “With Me to Lebanon you shall come”: to say, from the time of your departure from here until the time of your coming here, I am with you wherever you go out and come in. That is, as stated above; understand well.

If you examine more closely, you will see wonders. For surely the yud of the aforesaid “וְאָנֹכִי,” which joins the expression “אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה,” from which comes the principal ascent—for it is what stood by us and our forefathers in our exile, not allowing the other side to spread even over it, etc., as stated above—this very yud joins in the first Name that emerges from this verse, which is אמ״י: the alef of the first “אָנֹכִי,” the mem of “מִצְרַיְמָה,” and this aforesaid yud, as stated above.

It follows that even at the beginning of the descent into exile, which is the aspect of “I shall descend with you,” and from the beginning of the first exile itself—which is the aspect of the mem, the first letter of “מִצְרַיְמָה,” which is the beginning of exile—immediately and at once the aforesaid yud is joined there. It is the final yud of the aforesaid second “וְאָנֹכִי,” from which come hope and ascent, as stated above; and the Name אמ״י is formed, as stated above.

All this is to make known and teach that even at the beginning of the descent into exile and at the beginning of exile, the aforesaid yud, from which comes ascent, immediately stood by us. It itself stood by us at the beginning of the descent and in exile itself, to guard us and save us so that we would not become submerged there, Heaven forbid. For the blessed Lord declares the end from the beginning, and as explained in the Midrash concerning the verse, “And it was at that time, and Judah descended,” etc.: before the first exile had begun, the final redeemer, who is Peretz, was born, etc.; see there. That is, as stated above; understand.

(Halachos of Shilooach HaKain [Sending Away the Mother Bird], Halacha 5, item 23)

כָּל אָדָם בְּכָל זְמַן צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה עֲלִיּוֹת וִירִידוֹת כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו, כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲלוֹת מִדַּרְגָּא לְדַרְגָּא כִּי אִם עַל יְדֵי יְרִידָה שֶׁקֹּדֶם הָעֲלִיָּה, כִּי הַיְרִידָה הִיא תַּכְלִית הָעֲלִיָּה כַּמּוּבָא.
pairs.en: Every person, at every time, needs to have many, many ascents and descents throughout all the days of his life. For it is impossible to ascend from level to level except through a descent preceding the ascent, for the descent is the ultimate ascent, as brought there.

pairs.en: Because of these descents, many have stumbled and fallen greatly, for at that time great strengthening is required, which is the aspect of holy humility in all its aspects. This is the aspect of the prolongation of the exile of the entirety of Israel, for exile as a whole is the aspect of a descent preceding ascent, in the aspect of what the blessed Lord said to Jacob when he needed to descend to Egypt in exile: “I shall descend with you to Egypt, and I shall also bring you up.” Particularly this final exile, concerning which it was said, “And she descended astonishingly,” etc., as stated above.

qualifiedAfter.en: Because of these descents, many have stumbled and fallen greatly, for at that time great strengthening is required, which is the aspect of holy humility in all its aspects. This is the aspect of the prolongation of the exile of the entirety of Israel, for exile as a whole is the aspect of a descent preceding ascent, in the aspect of what the blessed Lord said to Jacob when he needed to descend to Egypt in exile: “I shall descend with you to Egypt, and I shall also bring you up.” Particularly this final exile, concerning which it was said, “And she descended astonishingly,” etc., as stated above.

pairs.he: וְכָל זֶה עוֹבֵר עַל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד בִּפְרָטִיּוּת, כִּי יֵשׁ מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְעוֹרֵר כְּלָל לַעֲלוֹת מִירִידָתוֹ וְיֵשׁ שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר קְצָת אַךְ מֵרִבּוּי הַיְרִידוֹת שֶׁעוֹבְרִין עָלָיו לְטוֹבָתוֹ כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה מִדַּרְגָּא לְדַרְגָּא, הַרְבֵּה נָפְלוּ עַל יְדֵי הַיְרִידוֹת [וכמובא מזה].
pairs.en: All this passes over each and every person individually. For there is someone who does not awaken at all to ascend from his descent, and there is someone who awakens a little; but because of the multitude of descents that pass over him for his benefit, so that he may ascend from level to level, many have fallen through the descents [and as brought concerning this].

pairs.he: עַל כֵּן צָרִיךְ שֶׁתֵּדַע שֶׁצְּרִיכִין הִתְחַזְּקוּת הַרְבֵּה וְעַקְשָׁנוּת גָּדוֹל כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ שֶׁל כָּל זֶה הוּא בְּחִינַת עַנְוַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין עַל יְדֵי שִׂמְחָה שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִבְּחִינַת נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע וְכוּ׳. וְעִקַּר הַכֹּחַ שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְחַזֵּק מִי שֶׁהוּא אֲפִלּוּ בְּתַכְלִית הַיְרִידָה, הוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין כֹּחַ מִבְּחִינַת הַגִּבּוֹרֵי כֹחַ עֹשֵׂי דְבָרוֹ לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּקוֹל דְּבָרוֹ, שֶׁהֵם הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּבוֹהִים שֶׁזּוֹכִין לִבְחִינַת נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע הָעֶלְיוֹן הַנַּ״ל, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת תּוֹרַת ה׳ וּתְפִלַּת ה׳ שֶׁשָּׁם הַחֶסֶד וְהַצְּדָקָה עַד אֵין סוֹף בִּבְחִינַת חַסְדֵי ה׳ כִּי לֹא תָמְנוּ וְכוּ׳, שֶׁזֶּה הַחֶסֶד מַמְשִׁיכִין בְּיוֹתֵר בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁהוּא חֶסֶד גָּדוֹל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר וְכַנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: Therefore you must know that much strengthening and great persistence are required. For the root of all this is the aspect of holy humility, which one receives through joy drawn from the aspect of “We shall do and we shall hear,” etc. The principal strength by which one who is even at the utmost descent can strengthen himself is by receiving strength from the aspect of “The mighty of strength who do His word, to hear the voice of His word.” These are the lofty righteous men who merit the aspect of the aforesaid supernal “We shall do and we shall hear,” which is the aspect of the Lord’s Torah and the Lord’s prayer, where kindness and charity are without end, in the aspect of “The kindnesses of the Lord, for we have not ended,” etc. This kindness is drawn especially on Roash HaShanuh, which is great kindness, as explained elsewhere, and as stated above.

pairs.he: כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהָבִין הַחֶסֶד וְהַצְּדָקָה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִשָּׁם, כִּי הוּא בְּחִינַת תְּפִלַּת ה׳ שֶׁה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ, כִּבְיָכוֹל, צָרִיךְ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל זֶה לְהַמְשִׁיךְ וּלְגַלּוֹת הַחֶסֶד הַנִּפְלָא הַנֶּעְלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיגוֹ, כִּי תְּפִלַּת ה׳ הוּא בְּחִינַת סִתְרֵי נִסְתָּרוֹת שֶׁבְּנִסְתָּרוֹת עַד אֵין קֵץ, כִּי הוּא בְּחִינַת נִסְתָּר הָעֶלְיוֹן הַנַּ״ל שֶׁאֵין מִי שֶׁיַּשִּׂיג אֵיךְ הוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹשֶׂה הַמִּשְׁפָּט בִּצְדָקָה וְכַנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: For in truth it is impossible to understand the kindness and charity drawn from there, for it is the aspect of the Lord’s prayer: the blessed Lord Himself, as it were, needs to pray concerning this, to draw and reveal this wondrous, concealed kindness that cannot be comprehended. For the Lord’s prayer is the aspect of hidden mysteries within hidden mysteries without end, for it is the aspect of the aforesaid supernal hiddenness, which no one can comprehend—how He, blessed be He, performs judgment with charity, as stated above.

For the Lord’s prayer is the aspect of hidden mysteries within hidden mysteries without end, for it is the aspect of the aforesaid supernal hiddenness, which no one can comprehend—how He, blessed be He, performs judgment with charity, as stated above.

pairs.he: וּבָזֶה יָכוֹל לְהִתְחַזֵּק כָּל אֶחָד בְּכָל עֵת, כִּי עִקַּר נְפִילָתוֹ הוּא מֵחֲמַת שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ שֶׁכְּפִי מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה חָטָא וּפָגַם מְאֹד, וְגַם כִּי חִזֵּק עַצְמוֹ כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה פְּעָמִים וְסָמַךְ עַל חַסְדֵי יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת נִסְתָּר, בְּחִינַת תְּפִלָּה, אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ פָּגַם גַּם בָּזֶה מְאֹד מְאֹד עַד אֲשֶׁר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אֶפֶס תִּקְוָה.
pairs.en: Through this everyone can strengthen himself at every time. For his principal fall comes from knowing that, according to the Torah’s judgment, he has sinned and caused great impairment; and also that he strengthened himself many, many times and relied upon the kindnesses of the Blessed One, which is the aspect of hiddenness, the aspect of prayer, but afterward impaired even this very, very greatly, until, Heaven forbid, there is no hope.

qualifiedAfter.en: Through this everyone can strengthen himself at every time. For his principal fall comes from knowing that, according to the Torah’s judgment, he has sinned and caused great impairment; and also that he strengthened himself many, many times and relied upon the kindnesses of the Blessed One, which is the aspect of hiddenness, the aspect of prayer, but afterward impaired even this very, very greatly, until, Heaven forbid, there is no hope.

pairs.he: אֲבָל כְּשֶׁמַּאֲמִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ תְּפִלַּת ה׳ שֶׁגִּלּוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה וְכַנַּ״ל שֶׁשָּׁם הַחֶסֶד וְהַצְּדָקָה עַד אֵין קֵץ הוּא בְּחִינַת נִסְתָּר גָּבֹהַ מְאֹד שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיגוֹ כִּי אִם גְּדוֹלֵי הַצַּדִּיקִים הַמֻּבְחָרִים שֶׁזָּכוּ לָזֶה, עַל יְדֵי זֶה גַּם הוּא יָכוֹל לְהִתְחַזֵּק בְּכֹחָם, כִּי הֵם מַמְשִׁיכִין עַנְוַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה גַּם עָלָיו וְכַנַּ״ל. רַק הָעִקָּר שֶׁמַּאֲמִין בְּכֹחָם הַגָּדוֹל וְיִהְיֶה עַז כַּנָּמֵר לְהַמְשִׁיךְ עַל עַצְמוֹ הָעַנְוַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מֵהֶם, כִּי שָׁם בְּעִנְיַן הָעַנְוַת הוּא הָעִקָּר מַה שֶּׁאֵין יוֹדְעִין מֵהֵיכָן הַהַתְחָלָה (וכמו שבאר במקום אחר סימן קטו). כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁמִּתְקָרֵב אֲלֵיהֶם יוֹתֵר נִמְשָׁךְ עָלָיו הָעַנְוַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה יוֹתֵר, וְכָל מַה שֶּׁמַּמְשִׁיךְ עַל עַצְמוֹ הָעַנְוַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה יוֹתֵר הוּא מִתְקָרֵב אֲלֵיהֶם יוֹתֵר, כִּי כָּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת. וְכֵן כָּל הַתּוֹרוֹת נָעוּץ סוֹפָם בִּתְחִלָּתָם וּתְחִלָּתָם בְּסוֹפָם וְיִתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
pairs.en: But when he believes that there is the Lord’s prayer, which our sages, of blessed memory, revealed, as stated above—where kindness and charity are without end, the aspect of exceedingly lofty hiddenness that cannot be comprehended except by the greatest of the chosen righteous men who merited this—through this he too can strengthen himself through their power, for they draw holy humility upon him too, as stated above. The principal thing is only that he believe in their great power and be bold as a leopard in drawing upon himself the holy humility drawn from them. For there, concerning humility, the principal thing is that one does not know where the beginning is (and as explained elsewhere, section קטו). For the more he draws near to them, the more holy humility is drawn upon him; and the more holy humility he draws upon himself, the nearer he draws to them. For all the words of this Torah—and likewise all the Torah teachings—have their end embedded in their beginning and their beginning in their end, and this will be explained elsewhere.

pairs.he: וְכָל זֶה זוֹכִין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בְּיוֹתֵר. וְעַל כֵּן הוֹלְכִין וְנוֹסְעִין לָבוֹא עַל קִבְרֵי צַדִּיקִים בְּעֶרֶב רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, כִּי נֶעְלָם מִמֶּנּוּ וְלֹא נוֹדַע מִי הוּא זֶה שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַמְשִׁיךְ הַחֶסֶד הָעֶלְיוֹן הַנִּפְלָא הַזֶּה בְּעֶצֶם יְרִידָתֵנוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב, וּרְאֵה אֶת עַמְּךָ מוֹרִידִים מַאי, כִּי אִם הַצַּדִּיקִים שׁוֹכְנֵי עָפָר שֶׁגִּלּוּ כָּל זֹאת וְזָכוּ לָזֶה לִבְחִינַת תּוֹרַת ה׳ וּתְפִלַּת ה׳ וְכַנַּ״ל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב, טוֹבָתִי בַּל עָלֶיךָ לִקְדוֹשִׁים אֲשֶׁר בָּאָרֶץ הֵמָּה וְכוּ׳.
pairs.en: One merits all this especially on Roash HaShanuh. Therefore people go and travel to come to the graves of righteous men on the eve of Roash HaShanuh. For it is concealed from us and unknown who it is who can draw this wondrous supernal kindness amid our very descent, as it is written, “And see Your people bringing down” [printed note marker מאי; tiny quoted wording held for native review]. Only the righteous men who dwell in the dust, who revealed all this and merited this, the aspect of the Lord’s Torah and the Lord’s prayer, as stated above. As it is written, “My good is not upon You—to the holy ones who are in the land,” etc.

"אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה"

(מ״ו, ד)

כָּל אָדָם בְּכָל זְמַן צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה עֲלִיּוֹת וִירִידוֹת כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו, כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲלוֹת מִדַּרְגָּא לְדַרְגָּא כִּי אִם עַל יְדֵי יְרִידָה שֶׁקֹּדֶם הָעֲלִיָּה, כִּי הַיְרִידָה הִיא תַּכְלִית הָעֲלִיָּה כַּמּוּבָא.

וּמֵחֲמַת אֵלּוּ הַיְרִידוֹת הַרְבֵּה נִכְשְׁלוּ וְנָפְלוּ מְאֹד, כִּי צָרִיךְ אָז הִתְחַזְּקוּת גָּדוֹל שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת עַנְוַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה בְּכָל הַבְּחִינוֹת. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת אֲרִיכַת הַגָּלוּת שֶׁל כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי כְּלַל הַגָּלוּת הוּא בְּחִינַת יְרִידָה שֶׁקֹּדֶם הָעֲלִיָּה, בִּבְחִינַת מַה שֶּׁאָמַר ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיַעֲקֹב כְּשֶׁהָיָה צָרִיךְ לֵירֵד לְמִצְרַיִם בְּגָלוּת אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה. וּבִפְרָט הַגָּלוּת הָאַחֲרוֹן הַזֶּה שֶׁעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר, וַתֵּרֶד פְּלָאִים וְכוּ׳ וְכַנַּ״ל.

וְכָל זֶה עוֹבֵר עַל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד בִּפְרָטִיּוּת, כִּי יֵשׁ מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְעוֹרֵר כְּלָל לַעֲלוֹת מִירִידָתוֹ וְיֵשׁ שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר קְצָת אַךְ מֵרִבּוּי הַיְרִידוֹת שֶׁעוֹבְרִין עָלָיו לְטוֹבָתוֹ כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה מִדַּרְגָּא לְדַרְגָּא, הַרְבֵּה נָפְלוּ עַל יְדֵי הַיְרִידוֹת [וכמובא מזה].

עַל כֵּן צָרִיךְ שֶׁתֵּדַע שֶׁצְּרִיכִין הִתְחַזְּקוּת הַרְבֵּה וְעַקְשָׁנוּת גָּדוֹל כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ שֶׁל כָּל זֶה הוּא בְּחִינַת עַנְוַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין עַל יְדֵי שִׂמְחָה שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִבְּחִינַת נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע וְכוּ׳. וְעִקַּר הַכֹּחַ שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְחַזֵּק מִי שֶׁהוּא אֲפִלּוּ בְּתַכְלִית הַיְרִידָה, הוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין כֹּחַ מִבְּחִינַת הַגִּבּוֹרֵי כֹחַ עֹשֵׂי דְבָרוֹ לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּקוֹל דְּבָרוֹ, שֶׁהֵם הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּבוֹהִים שֶׁזּוֹכִין לִבְחִינַת נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע הָעֶלְיוֹן הַנַּ״ל, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת תּוֹרַת ה׳ וּתְפִלַּת ה׳ שֶׁשָּׁם הַחֶסֶד וְהַצְּדָקָה עַד אֵין סוֹף בִּבְחִינַת חַסְדֵי ה׳ כִּי לֹא תָמְנוּ וְכוּ׳, שֶׁזֶּה הַחֶסֶד מַמְשִׁיכִין בְּיוֹתֵר בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁהוּא חֶסֶד גָּדוֹל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר וְכַנַּ״ל.

כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהָבִין הַחֶסֶד וְהַצְּדָקָה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִשָּׁם, כִּי הוּא בְּחִינַת תְּפִלַּת ה׳ שֶׁה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ, כִּבְיָכוֹל, צָרִיךְ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל זֶה לְהַמְשִׁיךְ וּלְגַלּוֹת הַחֶסֶד הַנִּפְלָא הַנֶּעְלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיגוֹ, כִּי תְּפִלַּת ה׳ הוּא בְּחִינַת סִתְרֵי נִסְתָּרוֹת שֶׁבְּנִסְתָּרוֹת עַד אֵין קֵץ, כִּי הוּא בְּחִינַת נִסְתָּר הָעֶלְיוֹן הַנַּ״ל שֶׁאֵין מִי שֶׁיַּשִּׂיג אֵיךְ הוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹשֶׂה הַמִּשְׁפָּט בִּצְדָקָה וְכַנַּ״ל.

וּבָזֶה יָכוֹל לְהִתְחַזֵּק כָּל אֶחָד בְּכָל עֵת, כִּי עִקַּר נְפִילָתוֹ הוּא מֵחֲמַת שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ שֶׁכְּפִי מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה חָטָא וּפָגַם מְאֹד, וְגַם כִּי חִזֵּק עַצְמוֹ כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה פְּעָמִים וְסָמַךְ עַל חַסְדֵי יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת נִסְתָּר, בְּחִינַת תְּפִלָּה, אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ פָּגַם גַּם בָּזֶה מְאֹד מְאֹד עַד אֲשֶׁר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אֶפֶס תִּקְוָה.

אֲבָל כְּשֶׁמַּאֲמִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ תְּפִלַּת ה׳ שֶׁגִּלּוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה וְכַנַּ״ל שֶׁשָּׁם הַחֶסֶד וְהַצְּדָקָה עַד אֵין קֵץ הוּא בְּחִינַת נִסְתָּר גָּבֹהַ מְאֹד שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיגוֹ כִּי אִם גְּדוֹלֵי הַצַּדִּיקִים הַמֻּבְחָרִים שֶׁזָּכוּ לָזֶה, עַל יְדֵי זֶה גַּם הוּא יָכוֹל לְהִתְחַזֵּק בְּכֹחָם, כִּי הֵם מַמְשִׁיכִין עַנְוַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה גַּם עָלָיו וְכַנַּ״ל. רַק הָעִקָּר שֶׁמַּאֲמִין בְּכֹחָם הַגָּדוֹל וְיִהְיֶה עַז כַּנָּמֵר לְהַמְשִׁיךְ עַל עַצְמוֹ הָעַנְוַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מֵהֶם, כִּי שָׁם בְּעִנְיַן הָעַנְוַת הוּא הָעִקָּר מַה שֶּׁאֵין יוֹדְעִין מֵהֵיכָן הַהַתְחָלָה (וכמו שבאר במקום אחר סימן קטו). כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁמִּתְקָרֵב אֲלֵיהֶם יוֹתֵר נִמְשָׁךְ עָלָיו הָעַנְוַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה יוֹתֵר, וְכָל מַה שֶּׁמַּמְשִׁיךְ עַל עַצְמוֹ הָעַנְוַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה יוֹתֵר הוּא מִתְקָרֵב אֲלֵיהֶם יוֹתֵר, כִּי כָּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת. וְכֵן כָּל הַתּוֹרוֹת נָעוּץ סוֹפָם בִּתְחִלָּתָם וּתְחִלָּתָם בְּסוֹפָם וְיִתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.

וְכָל זֶה זוֹכִין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בְּיוֹתֵר. וְעַל כֵּן הוֹלְכִין וְנוֹסְעִין לָבוֹא עַל קִבְרֵי צַדִּיקִים בְּעֶרֶב רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, כִּי נֶעְלָם מִמֶּנּוּ וְלֹא נוֹדַע מִי הוּא זֶה שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַמְשִׁיךְ הַחֶסֶד הָעֶלְיוֹן הַנִּפְלָא הַזֶּה בְּעֶצֶם יְרִידָתֵנוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב, וּרְאֵה אֶת עַמְּךָ מוֹרִידִים מַאי, כִּי אִם הַצַּדִּיקִים שׁוֹכְנֵי עָפָר שֶׁגִּלּוּ כָּל זֹאת וְזָכוּ לָזֶה לִבְחִינַת תּוֹרַת ה׳ וּתְפִלַּת ה׳ וְכַנַּ״ל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב, טוֹבָתִי בַּל עָלֶיךָ לִקְדוֹשִׁים אֲשֶׁר בָּאָרֶץ הֵמָּה וְכוּ׳.

(הלכות מתנה הלכה ה׳ אות י״א)
breslov.en:
“I shall descend with you to Egypt, and I shall also bring you up.”

(46:4)

Every person, at every time, needs to have many, many ascents and descents throughout all the days of his life. For it is impossible to ascend from level to level except through a descent preceding the ascent, for the descent is the ultimate ascent, as brought there.

Because of these descents, many have stumbled and fallen greatly, for at that time great strengthening is required, which is the aspect of holy humility in all its aspects. This is the aspect of the prolongation of the exile of the entirety of Israel, for exile as a whole is the aspect of a descent preceding ascent, in the aspect of what the blessed Lord said to Jacob when he needed to descend to Egypt in exile: “I shall descend with you to Egypt, and I shall also bring you up.” Particularly this final exile, concerning which it was said, “And she descended astonishingly,” etc., as stated above.

All this passes over each and every person individually. For there is someone who does not awaken at all to ascend from his descent, and there is someone who awakens a little; but because of the multitude of descents that pass over him for his benefit, so that he may ascend from level to level, many have fallen through the descents [and as brought concerning this].

Therefore you must know that much strengthening and great persistence are required. For the root of all this is the aspect of holy humility, which one receives through joy drawn from the aspect of “We shall do and we shall hear,” etc. The principal strength by which one who is even at the utmost descent can strengthen himself is by receiving strength from the aspect of “The mighty of strength who do His word, to hear the voice of His word.” These are the lofty righteous men who merit the aspect of the aforesaid supernal “We shall do and we shall hear,” which is the aspect of the Lord’s Torah and the Lord’s prayer, where kindness and charity are without end, in the aspect of “The kindnesses of the Lord, for we have not ended,” etc. This kindness is drawn especially on Roash HaShanuh, which is great kindness, as explained elsewhere, and as stated above.

For in truth it is impossible to understand the kindness and charity drawn from there, for it is the aspect of the Lord’s prayer: the blessed Lord Himself, as it were, needs to pray concerning this, to draw and reveal this wondrous, concealed kindness that cannot be comprehended. For the Lord’s prayer is the aspect of hidden mysteries within hidden mysteries without end, for it is the aspect of the aforesaid supernal hiddenness, which no one can comprehend—how He, blessed be He, performs judgment with charity, as stated above.

Through this everyone can strengthen himself at every time. For his principal fall comes from knowing that, according to the Torah’s judgment, he has sinned and caused great impairment; and also that he strengthened himself many, many times and relied upon the kindnesses of the Blessed One, which is the aspect of hiddenness, the aspect of prayer, but afterward impaired even this very, very greatly, until, Heaven forbid, there is no hope.

But when he believes that there is the Lord’s prayer, which our sages, of blessed memory, revealed, as stated above—where kindness and charity are without end, the aspect of exceedingly lofty hiddenness that cannot be comprehended except by the greatest of the chosen righteous men who merited this—through this he too can strengthen himself through their power, for they draw holy humility upon him too, as stated above. The principal thing is only that he believe in their great power and be bold as a leopard in drawing upon himself the holy humility drawn from them. For there, concerning humility, the principal thing is that one does not know where the beginning is (and as explained elsewhere, section קטו). For the more he draws near to them, the more holy humility is drawn upon him; and the more holy humility he draws upon himself, the nearer he draws to them. For all the words of this Torah—and likewise all the Torah teachings—have their end embedded in their beginning and their beginning in their end, and this will be explained elsewhere.

One merits all this especially on Roash HaShanuh. Therefore people go and travel to come to the graves of righteous men on the eve of Roash HaShanuh. For it is concealed from us and unknown who it is who can draw this wondrous supernal kindness amid our very descent, as it is written, “And see Your people bringing down” [printed note marker מאי; tiny quoted wording held for native review]. Only the righteous men who dwell in the dust, who revealed all this and merited this, the aspect of the Lord’s Torah and the Lord’s prayer, as stated above. As it is written, “My good is not upon You—to the holy ones who are in the land,” etc.

(Halachos of Matunuh [Gift], Halacha 5, item 11)

מהרח״ו ז״ל בטעמי המצוות (פרשת קדושים במצות ואהבת לרעך כמוך) כתב: דע כי כל ישראל סוד גוף אחד של נשמת אדה״ר וכל א׳ מישראל הוא אבר פרטי, כי זה הערבות שאדם ערב בשביל חבירו אם יחטא. ולכן נהג מורי האר״י זלה״ה לומר פרטי הוידוים כלם אפילו שלא היה בו, והוא אומר כי אע״פ שלא מצאו בו צריך להתודות עליהם. ולכן תקנו בלשון רבים ׳חטאנו׳ וכו׳ ולא ׳חטאתי׳ כי כל ישראל גוף אחד ולכן אבר שאין בו אותו עון ראוי להתודות, כי כשחטא חבירו כאילו עשהו בעצמו ולכן נאמר בלשון רבים. ע״כ.
pairs.en: MHRChV, of blessed memory, in Taamay HaMitzvos (the portion Kidoashim, in the commandment “You shall love your fellow as yourself”), wrote: Know that all Israel is the secret of one body of the soul of Adam the first man, and each individual of Israel is a particular limb; for this is the mutual responsibility whereby a person is responsible for his fellow if he sins. Therefore my master, the Ari, may his memory be for the life of the World to Come, was accustomed to say all the particulars of the confessions, even those that were not in him. He says that, although they did not find them in him, he must confess them. Therefore they instituted them in the plural: “We have sinned,” etc., and not “I have sinned,” for all Israel is one body; therefore a limb in which that transgression is absent ought to confess, for when his fellow has sinned, it is as though he did it himself. Therefore it is said in the plural. End of quotation.

וז״ל רבינו שם בליקוטי מוהר״ן: כל נפש מישראל הוא מושרש בשבעים נפש של בית יעקב. ושבעים נפש של בית יעקב מושרשים בשבעים פנים של תורה, וזה לעומת זה עשה האלקים, שכנגד שבעים נפש של בית יעקב הם שבעים לשון. שכל לשון ולשון יש לה מדה רעה בפני עצמה מה שאין בחברתה. ומחמת המדות האלו הם מרוחקים משבעים פנים של תורה. וכשהנפש של בית יעקב באה בגלות תחת יד שבעים לשונות, היינו במדותיהם הרעים. אזי היא ראמת שבעין קלין. כיולדת שקודם הלידה היא צועקת שבעין קלין כנגד שבעין תיבין שבמזמור ״יענך״, שבלעדי זה אי אפשר לה לילד. וזה כלל שכל נפש מישראל קודם שיש לה התגלות בתורה ובעבודה, אזי מנסין ומצרפים את הנפש בגלות של שבעים לשון, היינו בתאוותיהן. וכשהיא באה במדותיהן בגלות, אזי היא ראמת שבעין קלין. כי התגלות היא בחינת לידה, כי קודם התגלות של תורה, אזי היא בבחינת עיבור. שהתורה היא נעלם ממנו. כעצמים בבטן המלאה והיינו בגלות במדות הרעות של שבעים לשון. כי הקליפה קדמה לפרי, ומי שרוצה לאכול הפרי צריך לשבר מקודם הקליפה. לכן קודם ההתגלות מוכרח הנפש לבא בגלות, היינו במדותיהם, כדי לשברם, ולבא אחר כך להתגלות וכו׳. לפיכך כשקורין פסוק ראשון של ק״ש צריך להעצים את עיניו,
pairs.en: And these are the words of our master there in Likutay Moharan: Every soul of Israel is rooted in the seventy souls of the house of Yaakov. And the seventy souls of the house of Yaakov are rooted in the seventy faces of Torah; and God made the one corresponding to the other, for opposite the seventy souls of the house of Yaakov are the seventy languages. Each and every language has a bad trait of its own that its fellow does not have. And because of these traits they are distant from the seventy faces of Torah. And when a soul of the house of Yaakov comes into exile under the hand of the seventy languages—that is, within their bad traits—then it cries seventy cries. Like a woman giving birth, who before the birth cries seventy cries corresponding to the seventy words in the psalm “May He answer you,” without which she cannot give birth. And this is a general principle: before any soul of Israel has a revelation in Torah and in service, the soul is tested and refined in the exile of the seventy languages, that is, in their desires. And when it comes into their traits in exile, then it cries seventy cries. For revelation is an aspect of birth, because before a revelation of Torah it is in the aspect of gestation, when the Torah is hidden from it. Like bones in the womb of the pregnant woman; that is, in exile in the bad traits of the seventy languages. For the shell precedes the fruit, and whoever wishes to eat the fruit must first break the shell. Therefore, before revelation the soul must come into exile, that is, into their traits, in order to break them and afterwards come to revelation, etc. Therefore, when reciting the first verse of K״Sh one must close one’s eyes,

pairs.en: And so wrote Moharn״T, of blessed memory, in the laws of Chanukah, law 3. And they wrote further in the holy books. In the portion Mikaitz, the Baair Mayim Chayim wrote: It is known that the entire principal purpose of Yosef’s descent to Egypt was only to make a straight path before the children of Israel, when they would come to dwell in Egypt for labor and burden, so that they could endure there and leave there without their souls sinking into the impurity and filth of Egypt, in its fifty gates, from which they would no longer have been able to depart forever, etc. And Yosef the righteous, through his righteousness, subdued this path before the children of Israel by standing in the trial with his master’s wife, and subdued that shell before the children of Israel. Thus, when the children of Israel would strengthen themselves in this matter they could overcome their desire, to shut the door before Lavan the Aramean; and a stranger would not approach them, for they are holy. End of quotation. And in the portion Vayigash, the Maor VaShemesh wrote: The Holy One, blessed be He, was arranging circumstances in the sales of Yosef, specifically because he is the mystery of the righteous one who guards the covenant; and specifically to Egypt, which is the thing and its opposite—the primary source of impurity, the nakedness of the land, steeped in lewdness. There the Holy One, blessed be He, tested him with Potiphar’s wife, and he withstood the trial and did not blemish the sign of the holy covenant. This would have been impossible for one of the other brothers, because perhaps they would not have withstood their trial. Specifically Yosef the righteous, who is the mystery of the righteous one who guards the covenant, can withstand this trial through guarding the covenant. He drew this matter into Egypt, beginning there the rectification of the covenant from the blemish of the first man. And the fathers became a sign for the sons, for afterwards the children of Israel followed in his footsteps in the land of Egypt, fencing themselves against forbidden intercourse: they fenced themselves and accomplished this rectification completely by rectifying the guarding of the covenant, and raised all the sparks until they made it like a deep pool without fish. Without Yosef, who drew this forth, the children of Israel would not have had the power to draw forth and rectify this; only through what Yosef the righteous drew forth could the children of Israel afterwards rectify it to its root and ascend from Egypt. And the redemption was through Yosef, through his beginning to draw forth this matter. This is what is stated in the Midrash concerning the verse “The sea saw and fled”: it saw Yosef’s coffin, etc. End of quotation. And further.

כמ״ש האריז״ל בעץ חיים (שער ל״ט פרק א׳): כי אז כתיב בלע המות לנצח שהם הקליפות אשר חיותם הוא בחי׳ המ״ן אלו שלא הובררו והם עדיין בתוכם ואם היו נבררין לגמרי היה מסתלק מהם כל החיות והיו מתים לגמרי וזהו ענין אין בן דוד בא עד שיכלו כל הנשמות שבגוף כי כאשר יכלה כל הנשמות הקדושות לצאת משם ועולין בבחי׳ מ״ן שמהם נוצרים הנשמות כנ״ל בתחלת הדרוש לא יהיה עוד חיות אל הקליפות וימותו ויתבטלו וזהו בלע המות לנצח כי הקליפות נקרא מות תתבלע ותתבטל לגמרי. וז״ש פרשת פקודי דף רנ״ח ע״ב, כד יסתיים גלותא במשיכו דרגלין ברגלין כדין יבא משיח כי הרי אלו בחי׳ המלכים הם אדם א׳ מראשו ועד רגליו אשר נטבע באלו הקלי׳ ובכל פעם ופעם שיש זווג עליון אנו מעלין ע״י תפלתינו ניצוצות הקדושה שבו בבחי׳ מ״ן וכאשר יתבררו ויעלו גם הניצוצין אשר ברגליו אז יושלם להתתקן כל אדם הזה אז יבא משיח וענין רגליו אלו הוא בעשיה שהוא בחי׳ רגלים ושם הוא סיום הקדושה שהוא המלכות הנקרא קץ הימין וכנגדו בקליפה אשר שם נקרא קץ הימים וכאשר יתוקנו הנשמות אשר נפלו עד שם אז יהיה זמן הגאולה. ע״כ. ושם בשער מ״א פרק ב׳. וכן בשער המצוות פרשת ראה ועוד מקומות.
pairs.en: As the Arizal wrote in Aitz Chayim (gate 39, chapter 1): For then it is written, “He swallowed up death forever,” which refers to the shells whose vitality is the aspect of these M״N that were not clarified and are still within them. If they were completely clarified, all vitality would depart from them and they would die entirely. This is the meaning of “The son of David does not come until all the souls in the body are exhausted”: when all the holy souls finish departing from there and ascend in the aspect of M״N, from which the souls are formed, as stated above at the beginning of the exposition, the shells will no longer have vitality and will die and be nullified. This is “He swallowed up death forever,” for the shells are called death: it will be swallowed and nullified entirely. This is what is stated in the portion Pikooday, folio 258b: “When the exile is completed in the drawing of legs in legs, then Messiah will come.” For these kings are the aspect of one person, from his head to his legs, who was submerged within these shells. And each and every time there is a supernal union, through our prayers we raise the sparks of holiness within him in the aspect of M״N. And when even the sparks in his legs are clarified and ascend, the rectification of this entire person will be completed; then Messiah will come. And the matter of these legs is in Aseyuh, which is the aspect of legs. There is the termination of holiness, which is the kingship called “the end of the right”; and opposite it in the shell that is there is what is called “the end of the days.” When the souls that fell as far as there are rectified, then will be the time of redemption. End of quotation. And there in gate 41, chapter 2. And also in Shaar HaMitzvos, the portion Ri’ay, and further places.

As the Arizal wrote in Aitz Chayim (gate 39, chapter 1): For then it is written, “He swallowed up death forever,” which refers to the shells whose vitality is the aspect of these M״N that were not clarified and are still within them. If they were completely clarified, all vitality would depart from them and they would die entirely. This is the meaning of “The son of David does not come until all the souls in the body are exhausted”: when all the holy souls finish departing from there and ascend in the aspect of M״N, from which the souls are formed, as stated above at the beginning of the exposition, the shells will no longer have vitality and will die and be nullified. This is “He swallowed up death forever,” for the shells are called death: it will be swallowed and nullified entirely. This is what is stated in the portion Pikooday, folio 258b: “When the exile is completed in the drawing of legs in legs, then Messiah will come.” For these kings are the aspect of one person, from his head to his legs, who was submerged within these shells. And each and every time there is a supernal union, through our prayers we raise the sparks of holiness within him in the aspect of M״N. And when even the sparks in his legs are clarified and ascend, the rectification of this entire person will be completed; then Messiah will come. And the matter of these legs is in Aseyuh, which is the aspect of legs. There is the termination of holiness, which is the kingship called “the end of the right”; and opposite it in the shell that is there is what is called “the end of the days.” When the souls that fell as far as there are rectified, then will be the time of redemption. pairs.he: קמו.

המגיד מקאזניץ ז״ל בעבודת ישראל (פרשת מקץ) כתב: הכתוב אומר ויצבר יוסף ב״ר, הם ר״ב ניצוצין. הרבה מא״ד, אותיות אד״ם שם מ״ה שעל ידי זה השם הוא התיקון למלכין דמיתו להעלות הניצוצין קדישין. עד כי חדל לספור כי אין מספר, ר״ל שאח״כ העלה אותם לבחינת אי״ן הם העולמות הרמים והנשאים שרשי הניצ״ק והרימם ונשאם ונטלם לעולמות הגבוהים למעלה ממספר וחשבון, וזה וילקט יוסף את כל הכסף, כי חלילה לזרע יעקב אבינו ע״ה ולצדיק יסוד עולם שיהיה מגמתו לאסוף ולצבור כסף וזהב כדרך המוני עם, רק היתה כונתו לשם שמים ללקט הניצוצות קדישין ואהבתם וחמדתם הנקרא בלשון כסף כי נכסוף נכספתה, ויבא אתם ביתה פרעה תחת ידו, וממילא אח״כ יקל לבני ישראל להוציא הניצ״ק המכונסין ואסופים ולעשות מצרים ככתוב וינצלו את מצרים. ע״כ.
pairs.en: The Maggid of Kozhnitz, of blessed memory, wrote in Avodas Yisrael (the portion Mikaitz): Scripture says, “And Yosef accumulated B״R”; these are R״B sparks. “Much”—M A״D, the letters A״D״M, the name M״H, through which name comes the rectification of the kings who died, to raise the holy sparks. “Until he ceased counting, for there was no number”: that is to say, afterwards he raised them to the aspect of Ayin, which is the high and exalted worlds, the roots of the Nitz״K, and lifted them and bore them and took them to the higher worlds, beyond number and calculation. And this is “And Yosef gathered all the silver”; for far be it from the seed of Yaakov our father, peace upon him, and from the righteous one, the foundation of the world, that his aim should be to gather and amass silver and gold in the manner of the masses. Rather, his intention was for the sake of Heaven, to gather the holy sparks and their love and desire, which is called in the language “silver,” for “you greatly longed.” “And he brought them into Pharaoh’s house,” under his hand; consequently, afterwards it would be easy for the children of Israel to bring out the Nitz״K that were assembled and gathered, and to make Egypt as it is written, “And they emptied Egypt.” End of quotation.
